title: RNN Basics — Build a Better Memory Gate
key_insight: LSTM and GRU cells use learned gates to decide what to keep, add, reveal, or forget. A more direct memory path helps gradients survive longer.
body:
## Build a Better Memory Gate

A plain RNN forgets an important clue from the start of a long paragraph before reaching the end.

LSTM and GRU cells use learned gates to decide what to keep, add, reveal, or forget. A more direct memory path helps gradients survive longer.

Bidirectional RNNs read both directions when the full sequence is available. They cannot be used unchanged for live generation that must not look into future tokens.
common_mistakes: An RNN treats every sequence position as unrelated.
Hidden state is always a human-readable sentence.
Padding should contribute to the training loss as real data.
